findings.quote: without checking that the body has already reversed direction and slowed back to the same speed by symmetry
findings.note: After the reversal at t = 3.5 s the body speeds up, it does not slow: it accelerates from rest back to 5 m s⁻¹ at t = 4 s. The numerical consequence is nil but the description of the motion is wrong.
findings.fix: without checking that the body has already reversed direction and returned to the same speed by symmetry, since t = 3 s and t = 4 s are equally far from the highest point at t = 3.5 s

notes: v(3) = +5 and v(4) = −5 m s⁻¹, so the speeds are 5 and 5 and the ratio is 1 : 1; the highest point is at t = 3.5 s and both instants are 0.5 s from it. The distractor flags on options 3 and 4 stand: a pairwise search over the two velocities, their magnitudes, the g = 9.8 values, the heights at 3 s and 4 s and the distances covered in the third and fourth seconds produced no plausible route to 2 : 1 or 3 : 2.
